name: Ezer
overview: Ezer was a male member of the tribe of Gad, noted as the first among the Gadites to come to David while he was at Ziklag. His arrival to David marks a significant moment of allegiance during a critical period in David's rise. This event is recorded in 1 Chronicles 12:9.
namesAndTitles: The name Ezer means 'help' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name that is not indicated as being given directly by God. This meaning aligns with his role as a supporter in the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Ezer as a descendant of Gad, linking him to one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ezer’s significance lies in his position as a leader among the Gadites who pledged loyalty to David at Ziklag. This act of support contributed to the consolidation of David’s followers and the strengthening of his leadership. His mention underscores the unity and commitment of the tribe of Gad during David's early reign.
